messages:
mira: Quick question — hitting weird behavior when I abort a streaming call from Node SDK. AbortController.abort() cancels on client but server keeps emitting and we get partial tokens. Anyone seen this with our Python SDK too?

alex: Hmm, haven't seen server keep going. Which model + streaming mode? is this with response streaming or chunked events?

mira: It's streaming text (delta) to our websocket-backed agent. Node SDK v2.3.1. If I call controller.abort() inside onData handler, the Node side stops but the server trace shows still sending. If I re-run same request from py client and abort, server stops cleanly.

sam: Could be the http client lib in Node not wiring the cancel to the underlying socket. Are you using fetch polyfill or native fetch?

mira: Using node-fetch wrapper via our SDK. Also auth token refresh might kick in — we saw a 401 + retry in logs. Maybe retry path doesn't propagate abort?

alex: That's plausible. Our retry layer wraps requests and spins up a new attempt on 401, and it won’t see the AbortController after the first attempt unless we forward the signal. We added a note but maybe not consistent.

mira: Minimal repro attached:
```js
const ctrl = new AbortController();
client.stream({ prompt }, { signal: ctrl.signal }).on('data', chunk => {
  if (someCondition) ctrl.abort();
});
```
server log: "stream chunk" continues for ~2s after abort.

sam: Try passing the same signal to our retry wrapper — i.e., ensure `attemptOptions.signal = signal` for each attempt. Also check node-fetch supports AbortSignal for retries.

gabe: FYI ci-bot shows a flaky e2e failing in pipelines that aborts after 10s but 1/10 runs hang. Probably related.

alex: Action: I'll add a unit test that simulates abort during streaming and verify we cancel sockets and prevent retries. sam can check python client for symmetry.

sam: Python uses requests-async + httpx; httpx handles CancelledError from async generator differently, so it stops the server. I'll audit and add a note to sdk docs about 'signal must be forwarded through retry layer'.

mira: Thx. Also Q: auth refresh flow — if token auto-refresh occurs while streaming, should we allow transparent retry or fail the stream?

alex: We should avoid transparent auth refresh mid-stream. For streaming calls we should fail fast (401 -> surface error) rather than reattach. We'll add a policy: streaming endpoints are non-retriable on auth errors. Non-streaming may refresh.

sam: I'll open PR to (1) forward signal through retries (2) mark streaming non-retriable for auth 401 (3) add e2e test that aborts and asserts no server churn.

mira: Great. ping me on the PR for review. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: created issue #4521 'abort-signal-forwarding-and-streaming-retry-policy'

alex: Thanks all.
